study type: Model development and validation study (retrospective data collection)
exposure: Maternal anthropometric data (e.g., ischial spine diameter)
Obstetric medical records (e.g., artificial rupture of membranes, fetal head circumference-to-maternal height ratio)
cohort: The study included 302 pregnant women who underwent examinations and deliveries at Southern Medical University's Nanfang Hospital.
finding: The LASSO-based logistic regression model demonstrated the best predictive performance for cephalic dystocia with an AUC of 0.914, identifying maternal ischial spine diameter, fetal head circumference-to-maternal height ratio, artificial rupture of membranes, and childbirth self-efficacy as key predictive factors.
mod_finding: The developed model can assist in selecting the appropriate mode of delivery.
